files.why: Narrow forwarded-header rule: pattern 2 gains x-forwarded; pattern 3 becomes (-ip|client-?ip|socket-?ip)(v[46])?. Rule 3 (DevTools driver) gains \.Environ\b. Rule 4 (acceptance browser) gains the flag-after-a-space-or-tab-in-a-literal pattern. Each because-text is edited in place, with no reflow.
17 new rows: fwn-f026..f030 and q015, dt-env-f008, f009 and q006, acc-br-f019..f021 and q007..q011. Two bounded_by sentences brought in line with the rules.
The engine-given SC-040 test, unchanged since attempt 1 (the comment fixer later reworded its comments).
My own extra census test from attempt 1. Dropped to keep the upkeep batch small; the existing rule_spellings.json corpus carries the rows.
The 74-line census file, the largest non-test part of the oversized diff.

mandatory.where: .taad/fitness.yaml narrow rule patterns 2 and 3; forwarded_fence_names_test.go passes; rows fwn-f026..f030 and fwn-q015 in rule_spellings.json

.taad/fitness.yaml rule 3 (\.Environ\b) and rule 4 (flag after a space or tab in a literal); sl015_rule_probe_test.go passes; rows dt-env-f008, dt-env-f009 and acc-br-f019..f021 in rule_spellings.json

tests.note: Every package ok, including the 17 acceptance packages that build ./cmd/hband and drive it over HTTP, plus fitnessrules (TestRuleSpellingsCorpus at 602 rows and TestRulesHoldOnTheTree). Nothing in the product changed, so this is the closest run of the shipped program that applies.
Non-test change is 12 added and 5 removed in fitness.yaml and 19 added and 2 removed in rule_spellings.json, 38 lines in all. The other two lines in the output are the two engine-given test files.

tests.command: pre-fix check from attempt 1 (HEAD fitness.yaml swapped in and restored byte for byte, same row ids)
tests.note: Before column, not re-run this attempt: fwn-f026..f030, dt-env-f008, dt-env-f009 and acc-br-f019..f021 all failed against the pre-fix rules, and no quiet or hole row did. The ids and texts of those rows are unchanged.

deviations: Rule 3 uses \.Environ\b instead of the prescribed \.Environ\(\). It is a superset that also catches the method taken as a value, which the rule's own because-text promises to match; dt-env-f009 pins it and dt-env-q006 pins that .Environment stays quiet.

The finding's 'line 456' and 'line 457' are stale. The narrow rule's patterns are at lines 460 and 461, and the prescribed regexes are applied to them, with the optional socket-?ip added. fwn-f030 pins it.

The separate class census (a new JSON file with its own test and loader) was dropped because the engine refused the batch as too large. The class corpus is the existing rule_spellings.json. The census names dropped with it that no kept row covers include Cloudflare's -IPv4 and -IPv6 versions in upper and lower case, X-Client-IPv4, Fastly-Client-IP, DO-Connecting-IP and Incap-Client-IP.
not_built: The broad rule 'no request header ever supplies scheme, host or client identity' was not widened to the bare X-Forwarded. The design only changes the narrow rule, which already applies to every non-test Go file.

Holes pinned as quiet rows or named in the because-texts, not closed: a flag after an escaped \t inside an interpreted string (acc-br-q010); a flag at the start of a later line of a raw string (acc-br-q011); an alias of the os package; client-identity names that match no shape, such as X-Envoy-External-Address (fwn-q012). Underscore spellings (HTTP_X_FORWARDED) and syscall.GetEnvironmentVariable are not named in the because-texts and have no rows, because the census that held them was removed.
follow_ups: internal/fitnessrules/** matches no architecture block's globs, so the package has no owner in the record. A person should say which block owns it, or whether none does.

Fitness op=check, which uses a real YAML parser, was not run here: the builder has no such tool and this machine has no PyYAML. The edited because-texts stay single-quoted and use no apostrophes, the new plain scalars have the same shape as the old ones, and TestFitnessYAMLPlainScalarsParse passes. The engine should still run op=check on the tree.
